issues: BUILD/gn-check breaker (highest confidence): //third_party/blink/renderer/core does NOT depend on //crypto by default, and core/DEPS does not allow +crypto. Including "crypto/hmac.h" from core will fail `gn check`/link. The buildGn text calls `deps += [ "//crypto" ]` OPTIONAL — it is mandatory, and core/DEPS must add `+crypto`. Brave only gets away without this because brave_session_cache lives in a chromium_src override with its own deps. Fixed in corrected diff.

Missing includes in farble_session_cache.cc: uses std::string_view (crypto Sign arg) and std::move but includes neither <string_view> nor <utility>. Usually transitively present, but not guaranteed and cheap to fix. Added.

BaseRenderingContext2D::GetTopExecutionContext() — the getImageData hook depends on this pure-virtual existing on the *base* class (not just CanvasRenderingContext2D). If it is only declared on the concrete subclasses, this fails to compile; fallback is to route through the canvas host. This is the single most likely source-file compile break and could not be verified without the tree.

crypto::HMAC::Init(const uint8_t*, size_t) and Sign(std::string_view, uint8_t*, size_t) — crypto has been migrating to base::span overloads. On a recent roll these raw-pointer overloads may be gone; if so, switch Init to base::byte_span_from_ref(token) and Sign to a base::span(digest) destination (needs base/containers/span.h). Left as-is (pointer form has been stable for years) but flagged.

WebGL hook: `pixels->byteLength()` assumes `pixels` is a raw DOMArrayBufferView*. If ReadPixelsHelper's param is MaybeShared<DOMArrayBufferView> (as some overloads are), it needs `.Get()`. Also the destination local being named `data`, the `offset` type, and `Host()->GetTopExecutionContext()` on CanvasRenderingContextHost all need confirmation against the tree. Marked PLAUSIBLE by the author; I agree it is the least certain hook.

CanvasAsyncBlobCreator ctor: reassigning the local `image` param is a no-op if the member (image_/static_bitmap_image_) is captured in the initializer list rather than assigned from `image` in the body. Also recent Chromium added a CanvasInterventionType/noise param to this ctor — confirm the `ExecutionContext* context` param still exists and consider integrating with, not duplicating, Chromium's own canvas-noise path.

All @@ hunk headers are approximate locators, not byte-exact context — this will NOT `git apply` cleanly and requires hand-placement of the getImageData/toDataURL/webgl/blob hunks. A compile-clean set of files still needs manual reconciliation with the target milestone.

Minor/non-blocking: SkImage::readPixels(pixmap,0,0) uses the context-less overload (fine for a SW image but deprecated in newer Skia); WTF::String::empty() (correct on current Blink, was IsEmpty() on older). Both acceptable on current main.

Scope-creep / duplicate-symbol link risk: this WebRTC-only patch also DECLARES and DEFINES kFarbleCanvas and kSpoofNavigator. base::Feature objects are external symbols; if the sibling canvas/navigator patches also emit BASE_FEATURE(kFarbleCanvas/kSpoofNavigator), the linker sees two definitions -> duplicate-symbol / ODR link error. A webrtc patch must touch only kFarbleWebRTC. Removed the other two in the corrected diff.

Namespace of the PORTALLOCATOR_* flags (and the PortAllocator return type) is unverified against the target branch. The cricket->webrtc merge in third_party/webrtc/p2p/base/port_allocator.h is mid-flight: on many still-shipping branches these constants resolve as cricket::PORTALLOCATOR_DISABLE_UDP/STUN/ADAPTER_ENUMERATION/DEFAULT_LOCAL_CANDIDATE, not webrtc::. If the branch still has them under cricket::, all four webrtc:: references fail to resolve (and the shown 'std::unique_ptr<webrtc::PortAllocator>' return type would also be wrong). The four flag names themselves exist and are correct; only the namespace is in doubt. Must be matched to port_allocator.h in the actual tree.

Block #1 depends on unverified context: it assumes a local named 'webrtc_ip_handling_policy' of type blink::WebString populated by Platform::Current()->GetWebRTCRendererPreferences(...). If that variable is std::string on the target revision (some revisions are), 'webrtc_ip_handling_policy = blink::WebString::FromUTF8(...)' is a type-mismatch compile error; the fix there is to assign the bare constant (webrtc_ip_handling_policy = blink::kWebRTCIPHandlingDisableNonProxiedUdp;). If the prefs-read path or variable name differs, block #1 assigns to a nonexistent identifier.

Anchors are placeholders (@@ -XXX / -YYY) and the middle policy->Config mapping is paraphrased in a comment rather than reproduced, so the diff will NOT apply to a real tree as written. Block #1 must sit immediately after the GetWebRTCRendererPreferences(...) call and before the if/else-if chain comparing webrtc_ip_handling_policy to the kWebRTCIPHandling* constants; block #2 immediately after the P2PPortAllocator is constructed and before 'return'.

Non-blocking but worth noting: set_flags()/flags() on P2PPortAllocator are valid here only because the allocator is not yet Initialize()'d (PortAllocator's thread check passes pre-Initialize); if a future revision recomputes flags inside Initialize(), block #2 becomes a no-op and would need to move post-Initialize. Not a compile error. modules_export.h / MODULES_EXPORT is the correct export for this tier and same-component use is fine.

BUILD.gn target is wrong -> hard link break. There is no third_party/blink/renderer/core/frame/BUILD.gn containing a blink_core_sources("frame") target. In current Blink the frame sources (navigator_id.cc, navigator_base.cc, navigator_concurrent_hardware.cc) are listed in the single third_party/blink/renderer/core/BUILD.gn with a directory prefix, e.g. "frame/navigator_id.cc". The two new files must be added there as "frame/antidetect_navigator_config.cc" and "frame/antidetect_navigator_config.h". As written (bare filenames into a non-existent target), the .cc is never compiled -> undefined reference to blink::AntidetectNavigatorConfig::Get() from all three hook files.

String::FromUTF8(std::string) is version-sensitive. It compiles on current main only via the FromUTF8(std::string_view) overload (std::string -> string_view implicit). On branches where FromUTF8 is (const char*, size_t)/(const char*) only, cmd.GetSwitchValueASCII(...) (a std::string temporary) will not bind. Portable form: String::FromUTF8(s.data(), s.size()). Likewise String::empty() is the current spelling (was IsEmpty()); fine on current main, breaks on older branches.

Trailing-context anchors must match the real bodies or the hunks fail to apply (git apply tolerates line offset, not context mismatch). Highest risk: NavigatorConcurrentHardware::hardwareConcurrency() may not be a bare `return static_cast<unsigned>(base::SysInfo::NumberOfProcessors());` on current Blink (can be clamped/routed differently), so that trailing context line may not exist verbatim. navigator_id.cc platform() anchoring on `#if BUILDFLAG(IS_MAC)` right after the brace, and features.h/.cc anchoring on `namespace features {` (may be collapsed `namespace blink::features {`) are also fragile. Apply with --recount / re-anchor.

Confirm exact declared qualifiers or you get a new overload instead of an override: NavigatorID::platform() must be declared `virtual String platform() const;` and NavigatorBase::userAgent() must be `String userAgent() const` (overriding NavigatorID's pure virtual). The patch's definition signatures match what I expect on current Blink, but a mismatch would fail to compile.

Functional (not compile): the patch only READS --antidetect-* switches. Nothing appends them per renderer. Without wiring ContentBrowserClient::AppendExtraCommandLineSwitches (or RendererPreferences.user_agent_override for the UA/UA-CH header surface), HasSessionToken() is always false and every hook is a silent no-op.
